classification.type: Vane-axial fan, direct drive, in-line motor

introduction.summary: An axial flow fan moves air parallel to its shaft. Aerofoil blades on a hub act like small wings: as they turn they push air along the casing. Outlet guide vanes remove the swirl the blades add, turning it into pressure. Axial fans give large flow at low-to-medium pressure and are used for ventilation, cooling towers, tunnels and (with variable-pitch blades) large boiler draft fans.

video_tutorials.title: Axial Flow Fan — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Axial Flow Fan.
An axial flow fan moves air along its axis with rotating aerofoil blades.
Each blade acts like a wing; the blade pitch sets the flow and pressure.
Guide vanes after the rotor remove swirl and recover pressure.
Typical applications include tunnel and mine ventilation; cooling towers and air-cooled condensers; HVAC supply/exhaust; boiler draft (variable-pitch axial fans).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Fan Casing (Tube) with Flanges & Supports, Inlet Bell (Bellmouth) & Guard Ring, Impeller: Hub & 8 Aerofoil Blades (adjustable pitch).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

The rotating blades push air axially and add swirl.

video_tutorials.title: Axial Flow Fan — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Axial Flow Fan.
Check vibration and noise.
Check blade pitch and tightness; clean blades.
Replace motor bearings; inspect blade roots.
Watch for stall / surge: noise, pulsating flow. Common cause: operating at too high resistance.
Watch for vibration: high vibration. Common cause: unequal blade pitch, fouling.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
